paths.title: Begin with Awareness
paths.blurb: Three short, non-sectarian books that move from noticing the mind, to stepping back from it, to staying steady when life is hard.

steps.why: A brief introduction to present-moment attention, with minimal jargon.
Builds on that idea with a practical account of inner patterns and how to let them go.
Adds a Buddhist perspective on staying present with pain rather than avoiding it.

paths.title: First Steps in Wicca & Folk Magic
paths.blurb: Start with a structured course, then a solitary-practice guide, then a broad reference. Note that Wicca is one religion; the reference book covers many traditions of folk magic.

steps.why: A lesson-by-lesson introduction to Wicca as a religion.
Cunningham’s guide for practising alone, with ritual outlines.
A browsable reference once you want to explore folk-magic traditions beyond Wicca.

paths.title: Entering the Nag Hammadi Texts
paths.blurb: Read the scholarly context, then a primary text. Gnostic literature is distinct from Hermetic and from orthodox Christian mystical writing.

steps.why: Explains what the Nag Hammadi library is and why it matters for early Christian history.
A Nag Hammadi text in a Forbidden Mantra Press edition.

paths.title: First Mantra Practices
paths.blurb: Begin with a general guide to Sanskrit mantra, then move to individual mantras from the Forbidden Mantra Series. Traditionally some mantras are received from a teacher; the books note this where they say so.

steps.why: A broad introduction with transliterations and instructions.
One of the best-known Vedic mantras, in a focused guide.
A mantra traditionally addressed to Shiva, studied in its own guide.

paths.title: Taoist Inner Cultivation, Carefully
paths.audience: Readers curious about Taoist energy practice
paths.blurb: A first look at modern Taoist cultivation. More titles, including classic translations such as the Tao Te Ching, are staged for verification and will join this path.

steps.why: A modern Healing Tao presentation of internal-energy practice.

paths.title: Tarot Foundations
paths.blurb: A single, durable anchor text that rewards re-reading. More tarot titles are staged.

steps.why: A card-by-card study that treats tarot as symbolic language.

paths.title: Fantasy: Where to Begin
paths.blurb: Five approachable starting points, from a school of magic to a quest to a classic archipelago. Each is the first or a standalone book of its story.
paths.disclaimer: Independent recommendations. Forbidden Mantra Press is not affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by the authors, publishers or rights holders of the books or franchises mentioned.

steps.why: The best-known modern school-of-magic story, and the first of its series.
A shorter, lighter quest that leads into The Lord of the Rings.
A concise story about power, balance and the importance of names.
A classic children's fantasy that adults still read.
A modern urban fantasy that begins in a recognizable city.

paths.title: After Harry Potter
paths.audience: Readers who have finished the Harry Potter books
paths.blurb: Books with schools of magic, hidden worlds or wry humour, plus the real history of magic behind the stories.
paths.disclaimer: Independent listing and recommendations. Forbidden Mantra Press is not affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by J.K. Rowling, her publishers or the rights holders of Harry Potter.

steps.why: The real traditions of magic, alchemy and folklore, from a British Library exhibition book.
Another young wizard's education, with a more reflective tone.
Magic returns to Regency England, written in the style of a period novel.
A comic fantasy about the end of the world.
A long, absorbing story that includes a university of magic.

paths.title: Philosophy for Living: First Steps
paths.audience: Readers new to Stoic and practical philosophy
paths.blurb: Primary texts and one modern classic on finding meaning, in translations aimed at general readers.

steps.why: Short, private reflections on Stoic practice.
Letters that apply Stoic ideas to everyday problems.
A modern account of finding meaning under extreme conditions.

collections.title: Stress, Emotion & the Body
collections.blurb: Books that approach inner life and physical wellbeing together, from a physician’s clinical view to contemplative guides.

collections.title: The Mantra Shelf
collections.blurb: Sanskrit mantras explained for practitioners, including the Forbidden Mantra Series.

collections.title: Modern Witchcraft & Wicca
collections.blurb: The core introductory shelf for readers beginning with Wicca and magical practice.

collections.title: Ancient Texts & Their Readers
collections.blurb: Primary texts and the scholarship around them: Nag Hammadi, the Kebra Nagast and Hindu epic material.

collections.title: If You Love Harry Potter
collections.blurb: Independent recommendations for readers of Harry Potter: more magic school and hidden-world fiction, the real history of magic, and folk-magic references.
collections.disclaimer: Independent listing and recommendations. Forbidden Mantra Press is not affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by J.K. Rowling, her publishers or the rights holders of Harry Potter.

collections.title: Major Fantasy Authors: Where to Start
collections.blurb: One recommended entry point for each of the best-known names in modern fantasy.
collections.disclaimer: Independent recommendations. Forbidden Mantra Press is not affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by the authors, publishers or rights holders of the books or franchises mentioned.

collections.title: Myth Retold
collections.blurb: Novels and retellings that bring myth and legend into fiction, with a folk-tale classic and one comparative study.
collections.disclaimer: Independent recommendations. Forbidden Mantra Press is not affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by the authors, publishers or rights holders of the books or franchises mentioned.

collections.title: Gothic & Supernatural Classics
collections.blurb: Haunted houses, vampires and uncanny carnivals, from the nineteenth century to the present.
collections.disclaimer: Independent recommendations. Forbidden Mantra Press is not affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by the authors, publishers or rights holders of the books or franchises mentioned.

collections.blurb: Stoic and existential classics in modern translations.
